title: Infinite Page Loading Next.js when no connection to search server
body:
### 🐛 Current behavior

Next.js version: 15.0.4

I'm using InstantSearchNext together with Typesense (`typesense-instantsearch-adapter`). Everything works fine, except when there's no connection to the self hosted Typesense server. In this case, the following things happen:

* Server side: A huge nested stack trace is displayed with this content:
  ```
  constructor: [Function: AxiosError] { from: [Function (anonymous)] },
  toJSON: [Function: toJSON],
  [AggregateError: ] { code: 'ECONNREFUSED' }
  ```
* Client side: Infinite loading screen.

Yes, this is problem is more relevant for self hosted search servers, but I would expect this behaviour to appear as well when there's a connection problem with Algolia.

### 🔍 Steps to reproduce

1. Install InstantSearchNext
2. Point the search client to a non-existing URL
3. Open the page with SSR enabled

I tried to replicate the local setup on codesandbox, but I see a different error there.

### Live reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/nifty-snowflake-fgxqcg?file=%2Fcomponents%2Fsearch.tsx%3A5%2C9-5%2C21

### 💭 Expected behavior

I would expect to see the Next.js error component being sent to the browser.

Could it be that the error is not bubbled up correctly? Or it's bubbled up, but some code is not reacting to it? I looked into this code a bit and was wondering if the reason is that the promise only resolved on "result": `once('result'`
https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/master/packages/react-instantsearch-nextjs/src/InitializePromise.tsx

I found this previous issue that sounds related to the current problem. The solution at that time was to adjust the error propagation logic: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/issues/5233

Thanks for any support on this issue!

### Package version

react-instantsearch-nextjs@0.3.20 react-instantsearch@7.13.9 typesense-instantsearch-adapter@2.8.0

### Operating system

maxOS 15.2

### Browser

Chrome 131

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct

comments.body: This is not a realistic use case as Algolia has a robust SLA, so an edge case happening while there's no network connection is so rare it won't happen in real life. You can likely catch the error in your adapter and work that way
Happy to accept a PR to reject in case of an error, it makes sense to forward the error. What does the waiting on the searchQueueEmpty do additionally? Isn't the result event equivalent?
Awesome! After some testing, the error event listeners are actually triggered when an error occurs and there is no need for listening on searchQueueEmpty. Thanks for bringing this up!

I've created a PR that reuses the waitForResults utility from InstantSearch core instead, which already has the error handling. Please check out the preview and let me know if this fixes the behaviour! https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/pull/6616
do you have a reproduction for this @peyronoscar? I feel like this may be another issue
Hmm yes something clearly is still wrong. Even with a catch the error seems to be very deep as if something retries, although the search function is only called once.
Indeed. The catch works as hack to get it working temporarily for me, but a deeper debugging will have to be done.

Hi everyone, what's the current status of this issue? I'm experiencing a similar problem in an app using [searchkit](https://www.searchkit.co/) with Elasticsearch as the client.

I've noticed that when the issue described here occurs, the Elasticsearch instance freezes. I suspect InstantSearch is launching infinite queries to it, which causes all search features in my app to stop working until Elasticsearch restarts.

Debugging this is challenging, so I'm working with limited information. However, knowing the status of this issue would help me move my investigation forward.

Thanks!
Did you try out https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/pull/6616? I didn't get any community feedback of users of other providers to see if this helps.
I've finally had some time to try the proposal on #6616, and it did not solve the issue. I still "freeze" the Elasticsearch instance due to the huge amount of requests sent by this problem.
Removing that line means that the search will not be waited for, meaning you likely have a client hydration mismatch @nx-alejandrolacasa

Hi! Thanks for the feedback. I know it's far from ideal, but functional nonetheless.

I’d rather have hydration issues than have a search page that throws down the search server...
In that case, I suggest you can use InstantSearch purely frontend, and use none of the next packages

Actually, I need the routing, as I update the URL when filtering and such, and I have created a component that redirects to the search page with certain filters applied. I need the Next.js stuff, sadly.

Hi @Haroenv. After some intense session with Claude Code, I've achieved to make it work properly on my project. I've created #6875 with the code that fixes it. In the end it is a more refined version of what others did before.

When there's not connection (or something fails between the client and the server), no infinite loop happens now, preventing from "frying" the server with multiple calls.

SSR worked perfectly for me, along with widget/refinements initialisation, etc.

All feedback is appreciated, thanks!

Following @Haroenv suggestions on my PR (thanks for your support), I've moved the fixes to the `searchkit` adapter: https://github.com/searchkit/searchkit/pull/1412.

After doing the changes, I must confess they feel more simple in there, which is always a good thing.

I am afraid that repo is not that well maintained as this one, so it may take time for the changes to be merged, but in the meantime I've used https://github.com/ds300/patch-package to patch the changes on my projects. They are working fine so far!

Sadly, I won't be able to do the same for the `typesense` adapter, I don't have the time and knowledge to build a demo project and try it for myself.
